Leave-one-out estimates of a difference in differences

Source: R/policy_plots.R
loounit.Rd

Re-estimates plndid leaving out one treated unit at a time, to show that no single unit drives the result.

Usage

loounit(data, unit, time, y, trtd, covs = NULL, cl = NULL, units = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

trtd

Column name of the treatment indicator (0 or 1).

covs

Optional column names of time-varying controls.

cl

Column name of the clusters (default the unit), or two column names for two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), each term with the small-sample factor of the dimension with fewer clusters, and t on its \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. A composite cluster (district by month, say) is one column made with interaction().

units

Which units to leave out (default every treated unit).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_loo: dropped, estimate, se; attribute full (the estimate with every unit). plot() draws the histogram with the full-sample estimate and a summary.

Examples

p <- polex()
l <- loounit(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "reformed")
range(l$estimate)
#> [1] -3.285556 -3.186253
plot(l)
